For each build scenario (e.g. Boot loader, ECU Application) an own set of memory mapping files has to be provided.

The memory mapping file name shall be {Mip}_MemMap.h for basic software modules and {componentTypeName}_MemMap.h for software components where {Mip} is the Module implementation prefix and {componentTypeName} is the name of the software component type.

Each AUTOSAR basic software module and software component shall wrap declaration and definition of code, variables and constants using the following mechanism: 1. Definition of start symbol for module memory section 2. Inclusion of the memory mapping header file 3. Declaration/definition of code, variables or constants belonging to the specified section 4.…

The memory mapping header files shall provide a mechanism to select different code, variable or constant sections by checking the definition of the module specific Memory Allocation Key Words for starting a section (see [SWS_MemMap_00038]). Code, variables or constants declared after this selection shall be mapped to this section.

The memory mapping header files shall provide a mechanism to deselect different code and variable sections by checking the definition of the module specific Memory Allocation Key Words for stopping a section (see [SWS_MemMap_00038]). The selected section shall be deactivated if the section macro is defined before include of the memory mapping header file. C…

The memory mapping header files shall check if they have been included with a valid memory mapping symbol and in a valid sequence (no START preceded by a START, no STOP without the corresponding START). This shall be done by a preprocessor check.
If a compiler/linker does not require specific commands to implement the functionality of SWS Memory Mapping, the Memory Allocation Keyword defines might be undefined without further effect.
The memory mapping header files shall undefine the module or software component specific Memory Allocation Key Words for starting or stopping a section.
The memory mapping header files shall use if-else structures to reduce the compilation effort.
The selected section shall be activated, if the section macro is defined before include of the memory mapping header file.
The selection of a section shall only influence the linker's behavior for one of the three different object types code, variables or constants concurrently.
Each AUTOSAR basic software module and software component shall support, for all C-objects, the configuration of the assignation to one of the memory types (code, variables and constants).

The SWS Memory Mapping is applicable for each AUTOSAR basic software module and software component. Therefore the implementation of memory mapping files shall fulfill the implementation and configuration specific needs of each software module in a specific build scenario.
